full_text_en:
1569 Rice Seed Growers of Yuanba Township and Nuli Township, Anyue County v. Anyue County Seed Company — dispute over rice seed production and purchase contract

Plaintiffs: 1,569 rice seed growers (hereinafter referred to as the rice seed growers) of Yuanba Township and Nuli Township, Anyue County, Sichuan Province.

Agents ad litem: Tian Anbang, Chen Yingjiu, Tian Dajian, Tian Zhongshun, Liu Guoqing, Dong Wenyou, Wu Enhua, farmers of Yuanba Township, Anyue County.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jinggao, farmer of Nuli Township, Anyue County.

Defendant: Anyue County Seed Company (hereinafter referred to as the Seed Company).

Legal Representative: Deng Maozhong, Manager of Anyue County Seed Company.

Litigation Representatives: Xiao Kaiyuan, Gao Daiquan, Legal Counsel of Anyue County.

On September 24, 1983, the plaintiffs, 1,569 rice seed growers of Yuanba Township and Nuli Township, Anyue County, Sichuan Province, entered into 63 contracts with the defendant, Anyue County Seed Company, for the production and purchase of Xianyou No. 2 hybrid rice seeds. The contracts provided: (1) The Anyue County Seed Company shall be responsible for technical guidance in seed production and shall timely provide parent seeds, standard nitrogen fertilizer (160 jin per mu, 1 mu = 0.0667 hectares), diesel oil, plastic film, pesticides, etc., as required for seed production. (2) After the rice seeds matured in 1984, the Seed Company shall purchase the seeds by exchange or at a negotiated price. For exchange, each jin of seeds shall be exchanged for 9 jin of paddy rice; for negotiated price, Grade A seeds shall be RMB 2.05 per jin, and Grade B seeds shall be RMB 2.00 per jin. After the purchase of seeds is completed, the Seed Company shall pay the full amount within 20 days at the price stipulated in the contract. (3) The rice seed growers shall follow the unified guidance of the Seed Company, with village groups uniformly planning isolation zones, uniformly planning winter crops and sowing time for seed production fields, uniformly planning male parent seedling sites, uniformly conducting female parent germination and household sowing, uniformly pumping water for plowing, and uniformly delivering seeds for sale at the designated time. (4) The distance between ordinary rice and seed rice must be at least 5 zhang (1 zhang = 3.33 meters). If other rice is planted within the isolation zone, the Seed Company has the right to cut it down, and the loss shall be borne by the rice seed growers. (5) For the winter crops of the seed production fields in the current year, only rapeseed and green manure crops may be planted; wheat is not allowed, and winter waterlogged fields shall not be used as seed production fields. (6) The purity of rice seeds must reach at least 97%; if the proportion of off-type plants exceeds 5%, the Seed Company has the right to impose a fine. (7) Before delivery, seeds shall be selected with clean water to ensure they are first dry, second clean, third plump, and fourth free from black smut disease grains. (8) The seeds retained by the rice seed growers for their own use shall not exceed 5% of the total seed output; except for seeds for their own use, all remaining seeds shall be purchased by the Seed Company, and the rice seed growers shall not allow seeds to flow out or be exchanged; otherwise, the Seed Company shall impose a fine of RMB 50 to RMB 200 per mu of seed production field.

After the contracts were signed, the rice seed growers strictly carried out seed production in accordance with the contracts.

On July 31, 1984, before purchasing the seeds, the Seed Company, without negotiating with the rice seed growers or lawfully modifying the contracts, drafted on behalf of the Anyue County People's Government the "Notice on the Purchase of Seeds of Two Hybrids (Hybrid Rice and Hybrid Corn) This Year," which stipulated the negotiated purchase price for hybrid rice seeds as: Grade A, RMB 1.59 per jin; Grade B, RMB 1.55 per jin. In August, the Seed Company purchased rice seeds at the price stipulated in the said notice. The rice seed growers were dissatisfied with the Seed Company's breach of contract in unilaterally reducing the purchase price, and in three days, less than 30,000 jin of seeds were delivered. Seeing this situation, the Seed Company propagandized to the rice seed growers that the seed price would be increased for purchase, and exerted pressure on the rice seed growers through administrative measures, warning that if seeds flowed out or were exchanged, fines would be imposed in accordance with the contract. Consequently, the rice seed growers actively delivered seeds to the Seed Company, and within ten days, delivered a total of 635,833 jin and 8 liang (635,833.8 jin) of Grade A seeds, and 1,001 jin and 5 liang (1,001.5 jin) of Grade B seeds, with Grade A accounting for over 99%, fully meeting the quality standards stipulated in the contracts. After the vast majority of rice seed growers had delivered their seeds, the Seed Company refused to pay according to the contract prices, insisting on paying at the prices stipulated in the "Notice," and decided that Yuanba Township and Nuli Township, which had histories as seed production bases of eight years and two years respectively, would no longer be used as seed bases.

Therefore, the rice seed growers filed a lawsuit with the Anyue County People's Court. In their complaint, they requested that the Seed Company act in accordance with the Economic Contract Law, compensate them for the loss of RMB 292,934 due to the Seed Company's unilateral reduction of seed prices, pay liquidated damages, and compensate for the work loss and travel expenses caused by the defendant's breach of contract, and also requested that the seed production bases not be changed.

After accepting the case in accordance with the law, the Anyue County People's Court served the complaint on the defendant.

The defendant, Anyue County Seed Company, answered: (1) The seed prices stipulated in the contracts violated the provisions of the County Government's document; therefore, the contracts are void. (2) At the time of seed purchase, the market price of rice seeds had decreased; if the contracts were performed at the stipulated prices, the Seed Company, by selling at a price including profit, would cause losses to more farmers using the seeds, harming the public interest; accordingly, the contracts should also be void. (3) The rice seed growers were informed that the purchase price would be reduced; they voluntarily produced and consciously sold the seeds, which should be deemed as their actual agreement to modify the purchase price stipulated in the contracts. Therefore, the Seed Company bears no liability.

After hearing the case, the Anyue County People's Court, on the basis of finding the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, conducted mediation in accordance with Article 97 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Due to significant differences between the plaintiffs and the defendant on the price issue, mediation failed to reach an agreement.

On March 12, 1985, the Anyue County People's Court held a public trial of the case in accordance with Article 103 of the Civil Procedure Law. After trial, the court held that the rice seed production and purchase contracts signed between the plaintiffs, the rice seed growers, and the Seed Company were valid. The Seed Company's unilateral change of the seed purchase price stipulated in the contracts through administrative measures without consultation constituted a breach of contract. The reasons were: (1) Article 17, Item 3 of the Economic Contract Law provides: "If the policy allows negotiated prices for products, the price shall be agreed upon by the parties." After the issuance of the "Notice on Implementing Partial Negotiated Purchase and Sale of Improved Crop Seeds" by the Sichuan Provincial Department of Agriculture and Department of Grain in 1982, negotiated prices for rice seeds were permitted. The prices stipulated in the contracts signed between the rice seed growers and the Seed Company were negotiated and agreed upon by both parties, fully in compliance with national laws and policies. Since rice seeds could be subject to negotiated prices, the defendant's defense that performing the contracts at the stipulated prices would cause losses to more farmers using the seeds was untenable. (2) Article 17, Item 3 of the Economic Contract Law further provides: "For floating prices or negotiated prices, the price stipulated in the contract shall be implemented." Article 28 provides that modification of a contract "shall be in writing" to have legal effect. Although the Seed Company orally mentioned that the seed price might be reduced, it did not lawfully sign a written agreement to modify the price stipulated in the contracts. Moreover, the rice seed growers expressed at that time that they did not agree to change the price and demanded continued performance of the contracts. The rice seed growers' delivery of large quantities of seeds constituted an act of strictly abiding by the contracts, not an agreement to the Seed Company's proposed price reduction. (3) After the state changed the system from unified purchase to contractual purchase of grain, it was stipulated that contracts for the purchase of grain, once lawfully signed and concluded, must be strictly performed. Any modification or rescission of a contract must be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Economic Contract Law. Neither party to a contract may unilaterally and arbitrarily breach the contract due to changes in market prices or other improper reasons, so as to ensure the purchase of grain under the contracts in the stipulated quantity and quality and fulfill the state plan.

After the court investigation and debate concluded, the defendant recognized that unilaterally changing the price stipulated in the contracts constituted a breach of contract and, in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, requested mediation. The plaintiffs agreed and, considering the actual situation of the decline in market seed prices, were willing to make appropriate concessions.

Accordingly, mediation was conducted under the auspices of the Anyue County People's Court. After negotiation, the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement:

1. The Seed Company shall make up 14 fen (RMB 0.14) per jin for the purchase price of rice seeds, i.e., the price for Grade A is changed to RMB 1.73 per jin, and for Grade B to RMB 1.69 per jin. The Seed Company shall pay an additional RMB 89,156.90 to the 1,569 rice seed growers.

2. Due to the Seed Company's breach of contract, calculated at 0.03% of the total amount of delayed payment, it should have paid RMB 18,000 as liquidated damages for delayed payment; the rice seed growers made concessions, only requesting the other party to pay travel expenses for petitioning and work loss allowance, so the Seed Company shall pay RMB 4,000 as liquidated damages to the rice seed growers.

3. The remaining 1,600 jin of rice seeds not yet delivered by the rice seed growers shall be delivered according to the quality stipulated in the contracts; the Seed Company shall pay according to the prices stipulated in this agreement.

4. The litigation costs of this case, RMB 4,906.61, shall be borne by the Seed Company.
